05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.visual_critic_note: Intentional GitHub-dark palette with restrained single-accent blue, smart ghost-bar technique, and clear typographic hierarchy (uppercase tracking labels, quiet axis ticks), but the charts occupy only the top ~45% of the viewport, leaving a large empty void that makes the layout feel unfinished.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Histograms use zero baseline, Y domain derived from data via d3.max, ghost-bar crossfilter pattern correctly anchors scale during filtering, and uniform bin thresholds are semantically appropriate; only minor issue is hardcoded X domains that would not adapt to different data ranges.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.stress_test_note: Every brush mousemove fires updateAll() which filters 2000 records and rebins+repaints all 3 charts with no RAF/debounce; the source parameter is accepted but never used to guard cross-view updates; reset calls brush.move on each chart re-triggering the brush handler 3 extra times; x/y scales are closed over with no resize handler so they go stale on window resize.
05-crossfilter-flight-explorer.cognitive_load_note: 3 linked histograms with a single monochrome palette, ghost bars for context, and a clear flight-count counter keep cognitive load minimal — the classic crossfilter pattern executed cleanly with no excess complexity.

08-small-multiples-seasonal.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme small multiples with harmonious blue/salmon/green palette, axes only on left column and bottom row, and subtly restrained gridlines — but the shared y-scale leaves spring/fall panels with flat lines hugging the bottom, and the 1.4px lines feel thin at rendered size.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.encoding_integrity_note: Shared y-scale with zero baseline and data-driven domain is correct for cross-panel comparison, but xScale is hardcoded [1,31] for all months regardless of actual month length, causing Feb/Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov to have trailing whitespace and breaking the subset robustness invariant.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.stress_test_note: The pointermove handler synchronously updates 12 crosshair elements, 3 dot markers, and tooltip innerHTML on every mousemove with no RAF coalescing or dirty-flag throttle; all other criteria (no transitions to interrupt, static scales, pointer events unify mouse/touch, no cross-view dispatch) are clean.
08-small-multiples-seasonal.cognitive_load_note: 12 panels, 3 visually distinct year lines (color + dash), shared scales, and a calendar layout make cross-panel comparison easy; crosshair broadcasting across all panels works at this count but dot markers only appear on the hovered panel, slightly limiting the cross-month read.

11-zoomable-treemap.visual_critic_note: Hand-picked palette with depth-driven opacity and a coherent dark IDE aesthetic show real design intent, but many leaf cells are too small to read without zooming, limiting immediate data legibility.
11-zoomable-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Treemap area encoding is correctly proportional to file size via data-driven `root.sum(d => d.size || 0)`, zoom correctly remaps scale domains to focused node bounds, and no deceptive encoding choices (no radius scaling, no truncated baseline, no dual-axis); minor: no key functions in data join but irrelevant for this static single-render pattern.
11-zoomable-treemap.stress_test_note: zoomTo() mutates x/y scale domains synchronously before starting a 720ms transition with no .interrupt() call, so rapid clicks cause in-flight transition callbacks to immediately use the new domain, producing coordinate jumps; no brush/touch/feedback-loop issues exist.
11-zoomable-treemap.cognitive_load_note: 8-hue palette is at the warning threshold but works as spatial territory markers rather than lookup, zoom interaction with label culling and breadcrumb navigation cleanly manages the ~400-node density, though the root view has many unreadable micro-cells that require drilling to resolve.

17-chord-diagram-trade.visual_critic_note: The screenshot captures the animation mid-flight — chord ribbons (the entire data encoding) are invisible, and the diagram is vertically cropped; the visible arcs show good Tableau10 color choices and typographic hierarchy, but the visualization is functionally broken as captured.
17-chord-diagram-trade.encoding_integrity_note: Chord layout correctly derives all angular extents from the matrix (no hardcoded domains), ribbon widths and arc lengths are proportionally honest, tick marks use correct angular interpolation, and tooltip aggregations (row/column sums) are mathematically accurate; no key functions in joins is a minor robustness gap but irrelevant for this static chart.
17-chord-diagram-trade.stress_test_note: highlight() and reset() call .transition() without .interrupt() on arcPaths/ribbonPaths/labels, so hovering during the ~1.6s staggered entrance animation (named 'arcs'/'ribbons') creates conflicting unnamed transitions that can cause jumping or NaN attributes; no brush/zoom means Update Storm, Stale Scale, and Infinite Loop checks are N/A; touch-vs-mouse is low risk given no drag interactions.
17-chord-diagram-trade.cognitive_load_note: 10-color Tableau10 palette hits the warning threshold but hover-to-isolate interaction effectively manages ribbon density (90 chords); screenshot captured before ribbons rendered so full density assessment is limited to structural analysis.

23-hex-bin-map.visual_critic_note: Deliberate plasma palette on dark background with sqrt-compressed color scale creates clear density gradients; state borders are appropriately quiet but the data-note text (#3d4155) is nearly invisible against the background.
23-hex-bin-map.encoding_integrity_note: Color encoding is honest (data-driven maxCount, uniform hex size, appropriate sqrt-power compression for skewed density), but the 20-bucket linear quantization used for rendering is not reflected in the continuous legend gradient, creating a minor mismatch between display and legend.
flags: Update Storm (slider `input` calls full `drawHexes` re-projection of 20k points on every tick without RAF or debounce)
Update Storm (ResizeObserver fires `redraw` including border re-draw on every resize frame without debounce)
23-hex-bin-map.stress_test_note: No transitions or cross-view dispatch to worry about, but the slider input and ResizeObserver both trigger expensive full canvas re-renders synchronously without coalescing.
23-hex-bin-map.cognitive_load_note: Single-view hex-bin map with a sequential plasma scale and one labeled slider control — minimal working memory demand, clear density clusters visible at a glance, and no categorical color overload.

35-color-palette-explorer.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed tool with clever contrast matrix (ratio text rendered in the actual foreground color), solid typographic hierarchy via small-caps panel titles, and polished palette switcher buttons — held from 8 by some cells where low-contrast ratios make the ratio numbers themselves illegible, which is ironic but still a readability issue.
35-color-palette-explorer.encoding_integrity_note: Bar chart correctly uses zero baseline (domain [0,100]) and key functions (.data(data, d => d.label)), but the x-scale domain is hardcoded to 100 rather than data-driven via d3.max, making it brittle under the scaling metamorphic transform.
35-color-palette-explorer.stress_test_note: Bar chart transitions (500ms enter, 400ms update) lack .interrupt() calls before new transitions, so rapid palette switching causes mid-flight snapping; no brush/zoom means Update Storm, Stale Closure, and Infinite Loop checks are not applicable, and Mouse-Touch Fight is minimal (click-only UI).
35-color-palette-explorer.cognitive_load_note: Three coordinated views (bar chart, contrast matrix, CVD strips) form a coherent conceptual unit with clear labeling and restrained layout; the 7×7 contrast matrix is dense but purpose-built for ratio lookup, not pattern reading.

41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme triptych with coordinated 5-color palette and consistent visual language across all three panels; radial bundling labels are too small/dense to read comfortably and chord ribbons at 0.2 opacity barely distinguish cross-group flows.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.encoding_integrity_note: No quantitative encoding violations (chord arcs correctly scale with connection counts, fixed-size nodes don't misrepresent data, no truncated baselines); minor imprecision in chord tooltip where cross-group edges are symmetrically double-counted into each group's 'total connections' label, which is standard but undisclosed convention.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.stress_test_note: Un-throttled resize handler fully rebuilds all three panels on every pixel of resize (full DOM teardown+rebuild with no debounce/RAF), and hover interactions use only mouse events with no touch disambiguation or event.preventDefault() guard.
41-force-bundling-chord-triptych.cognitive_load_note: Three well-coordinated panels with a 5-color palette and cross-panel highlighting keep cognitive load manageable, but the radial bundling center creates a visible tangle and 40 node labels at 9px crowd the ring — interaction is essential for disambiguation.

47-mixed-scale-parcoords.visual_critic_note: Dark navy background with Tableau10 categorical palette creates strong visual hierarchy and readable parallel coordinates, though line density at 0.32 alpha causes the unfiltered view to look murky and the scale-badge annotations feel visually underdeveloped.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.encoding_integrity_note: Mixed scales are clearly badged, domains are data-driven via d3.extent, log scale is appropriate for salary, and axes remain stable during brushing; only minor issue is hardcoded log tick candidates that could leave sparse ticks if salary range shifts significantly.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.stress_test_note: Brush fires drawCanvas() (300-line canvas redraw) on every mousemove with no RAF or debounce; ResizeObserver also lacks debounce; brush extents stored in pixel space become stale after resize, silently corrupting filter logic.
47-mixed-scale-parcoords.cognitive_load_note: 6 axes, 6 Tableau10 colors, and 300 lines at 32% alpha stay within cognitive limits — the ordinal Department/Performance axes create readable fan structure, though the unfiltered line density makes individual path tracing difficult without brushing.

49-textured-network-diagram.visual_critic_note: Intentional Julesz texton encoding with harmonious muted palette, clean sidebar hierarchy, and thoughtful grayscale toggle — let down only slightly by the node patterns reading as visually busy at this density.
49-textured-network-diagram.encoding_integrity_note: Categorical-only encoding (community via dual color+texture channels) is honest with no quantitative deception; fixed node radii encode no data; minor robustness gap from missing key functions in node/link data joins but inconsequential for this static dataset.
49-textured-network-diagram.stress_test_note: updateHulls() performs a full 6-path DOM join with 5 attribute mutations on every simulation tick (no RAF/dirty-flag), causing an update storm during drag when alphaTarget(0.3) drives rapid ticks; d3.drag() also lacks an event filter to prevent mouse/touch double-trigger on mobile.
49-textured-network-diagram.cognitive_load_note: 50 nodes with 6 well-separated clusters are immediately readable — dual color+texture encoding, convex hull overlays, and a restrained 6-color palette all manage complexity effectively, though animation quality can't be assessed from the static screenshot.

79-reduced-motion-dashboard.visual_critic_note: Dark GitHub-inspired theme and ghost/active crossfilter layering show design intent, but the histogram and revenue charts are flat single-color fills (uniform blue and green), the axis tick labels are nearly invisible (#3d444d on near-black), and a large empty space below the dashboard makes the layout feel unfinished.
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.encoding_integrity_note: All bar charts use zero baselines with data-driven Y domains, scatter uses key functions for object constancy, no size-encoding deception, and crossfilter axes stay fixed during filtering — only minor issue is scatter axes hardcoded to [0,100] (appropriate for this synthetic dataset).
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.stress_test_note: The brush 'brush' event calls updateAll() directly on every mousemove with no RAF/debounce, triggering transitions on 300+ scatter circles and all histogram/timeseries bars simultaneously, and none of the update functions call .interrupt() before starting new transitions, causing mid-flight snap on rapid input.
79-reduced-motion-dashboard.cognitive_load_note: 3-view crossfilter with 5 perceptually distinct colors on a dark background — density in the 300-point scatter is manageable because ghost dots provide context and the layout clearly separates scatter (brush) from histogram/timeseries (click filters), keeping working memory load low.

86-block-skill-matrix.visual_critic_note: Intentional dark theme with a consistent 7-category color system applied across cells, headers, frequency bars, and legend shows real design thought, but row labels at #667 on #111318 are nearly illegible and the 105-row density makes the matrix unreadable without interaction.
86-block-skill-matrix.encoding_integrity_note: Matrix uses honest binary presence/absence encoding, categorical color, and frequency bars with a data-driven zero-baseline scale (domain([0, d3.max(...)]) ); full redraw pattern sidesteps key-function issues, and no size, dual-axis, or smoothing deceptions are present.
86-block-skill-matrix.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, or transitions means the five major interaction traps are all avoided; the only minor concern is unguarded touch events on mobile, but with no scroll/zoom conflict the practical risk is negligible.
86-block-skill-matrix.cognitive_load_note: 7-color category palette and hover highlighting manage the 105×26 matrix well as a single conceptual unit, but 11px cells with 9.5px truncated row labels make individual block identification nearly impossible without hovering, pushing too much work onto interaction for a static read.

87-skill-anatomy-treemap.visual_critic_note: Deliberate dark-theme palette (Tableau 10 with opacity), clean typographic hierarchy, and well-padded treemap layout feel intentional, but category labels at 9px/35% opacity are barely readable in context.
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Treemap correctly encodes area proportional to line count via d3.hierarchy().sum(), uses data-driven layout with no hardcoded domains, and categorical color is ordinal — no baseline, lie factor, or dual-axis violations; full DOM teardown on resize makes key functions unnecessary.
flags: Update Storm (ResizeObserver calls full render() with chartEl.innerHTML='' on every resize event, no debounce or RAF)
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom/transitions so most interaction traps are N/A, but the un-debounced ResizeObserver triggers a full SVG teardown and rebuild at resize frequency, which will cause jank during window drag-resize.
87-skill-anatomy-treemap.cognitive_load_note: 8 categories with perceptually distinct colors, clear group borders and labels, and well-sized leaf cells with inline name+line-count labels keep the treemap readable at a glance; the only friction is a few small cells (e.g. cognitive-load, sharpen-tool) where labels are truncated and size differences between categories are hard to compare precisely.

90-skill-growth-sparklines.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dashboard with a Tableau-10-inspired categorical palette, clear typographic hierarchy, category badges with dot+label encoding, and crisp inline sparklines with area fills — held back from 9 only by the sparklines being quite small (88×26px) and the score mini-bars adding visual noise without much payoff.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.encoding_integrity_note: Shared-scale mode correctly anchors area fill at zero (domain [0,100]), score bars are properly zero-based, and per-skill domains are data-driven via d3.extent; main weakness is per-skill mode sets area y0 to local minimum minus padding rather than 0, creating a truncated baseline that exaggerates growth magnitude in the area fill.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.stress_test_note: No brush, zoom, or drag interactions exist; all re-renders fire on discrete click events only, so none of the five interaction traps (update storm, infinite loop, stale closure, mid-flight snap, mouse-touch fight) apply.
90-skill-growth-sparklines.cognitive_load_note: 26-row sparkline table with 7 category colors is well-managed: color is encoded redundantly via badges and sparklines, the shared-scale toggle and category filters reduce simultaneous load, and the tabular layout makes row-by-row scanning natural rather than overwhelming.

98-shape-morphing-timeline.visual_critic_note: Deliberately designed dark-theme demo with a coordinated quarterly palette (blue/green/orange/pink), confident typographic hierarchy, minimal dashed gridlines, and rich interaction (scrubber, play, pills, keyboard, tooltip) — held back from 8 by the vestigial 'bar' morph-label artifact and quarterly color encoding that adds visual noise without encoding information the x-axis labels don't already provide.
98-shape-morphing-timeline.encoding_integrity_note: Zero baseline correct for bars/area, scaleSqrt used for scatter size encoding, data-driven yScale domain, key functions present on joins; minor robustness gap: no line.defined() guard for missing values in line/area modes.
98-shape-morphing-timeline.stress_test_note: animateScrubberTo has no cancel handle so rapid pill clicks spawn concurrent RAF loops fighting applyT simultaneously, and the scrubber input event drives morphRender synchronously on every tick with no RAF coalescing.
98-shape-morphing-timeline.cognitive_load_note: Single view with 4 perceptually distinct quarter colors and clean bar layout reads clearly; main untestable risk is whether the scrubber-driven morphing (bar→line→area→scatter) maintains object constancy in motion, and the scrubber's dual role — controlling both chart-type morph and the month label — conflates two things without visual distinction.
